title: An Uneasy US-China Truce Rolls On
text:
An Uneasy US-China Truce Rolls On

Arthur Kroeber

Gavekal Research | 28 Sep 2026

As expected, very little of substance emerged from Thursday’s summit meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping. The two leaders extended the tariff and export-control truce by two months, to January 10, agreed to meet twice more before then on the sidelines of the APEC and G20 summits and established an artificial-intelligence dialogue that is likely to be as (un)productive as the Boards of Trade and Investment announced at the previous summit.This result is satisfactory for Xi, whose short-run objective is to show that the relationship with the US is stable and under control as he prepares the scenery for the 21st Party Congress about a year from now. And it is fine for Trump, who seems to have lost interest in either a confrontation or a grand bargain with China.
